description.narrative: (Sri Lanka): The 2022 protests in Sri Lanka highlighted the urgency that Sri Lankans place on political reform and the importance of parliamentary oversight functions. Through the Inclusive Participatory Process (IPP) activity, USAID will build the capacity of the parliament of Sri Lanka and multi-political parties and civil society organizations to improve the political and civic participation of women, youth, and under-represented groups. IPP will also provide technical support to the Election Commission (EC) to safeguard transparent and inclusive electoral processes.With FY 2022 funding, IPP will assist the EC in developing civic and voter education material and carrying out voter awareness campaigns. Through IPP, USAID will train 25 youth and 75 women representing multiple political parties and civic groups on political and civic participation. Should elections be declared, IPP will also award two subgrants to local organizations to conduct short-term and long-term election observation missions for the local and parliamentary elections.Through this activity, USAID advances the US Embassy's Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 2.2: 'Build support for adherence to rule-of-law, transparency, and inclusive governance' and the USAID Country Development Cooperation Strategy Development Objective 1: 'Effective Democratic Governance Strengthened.'$2,000,000 within this IM will contribute to the required DRG directive of $15,100,000.
